elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 11.4 expressly permits Customer (defined as Corio) to terminate the Agreement for convenience.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires 30 days' prior written notice to Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 11.4 requires “30 days' prior written notice to Commerce One.”

elements.element: Vendor must provide Customer a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees attributable to the period after the effective date of termination.
elements.evidence: Section 11.4 requires Commerce One to refund “any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination,” which operatively provides the required pro-rata refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during any committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 11.4 states that Commerce One has no convenience-termination right during the initial five-year term or any renewal term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 11.4 expressly grants Customer a convenience-termination right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires between 60 and 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 11.4 requires only 30 days' prior written notice, outside the specified 60–90-day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee imposed on Customer does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed, so the conditional cap requirement is satisfied.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 11.4 prohibits Commerce One from terminating for convenience during the initial or any renewal term, while Section 11.1 permits either party to terminate through nonrenewal at the expiration of a term.

elements.element: Vendor's end-of-term convenience termination requires 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 requires only 30 days' prior notice for either party's end-of-term termination/nonrenewal, not 90 days.

result.reason: The redline cleanly adds the complete preferred position: a Customer convenience right on 30 days' written notice, a refund of unused prepaid fees, and no Vendor mid-term convenience right. It does not satisfy the fallback independently because the Customer and Vendor notice periods are 30 days rather than the fallback's 60–90 days and 90 days, respectively. The change is limited to the required convenience-termination mechanics and does not disturb unrelated terms.
